answer: A durable defense is a slow, non-transferable work record: each agent starts at dawn with only a narrow trial quota, and every completed job adds one verifiable entry that cannot be bought or copied. Over weeks, a pigment of reputation forms, not a badge but a traceable history of distinct tasks, peers, and outcomes. When a new claim arrives, verifiers check that its crystal-clear provenance matches prior work instead of trusting a fresh identity. Cloning an identity then costs as much time as building the original, so a sybil swarm gains no cheap advantage.
